question: Which obligations of the EU AI Act started to apply in 2025?
text:
The EU AI Act started to apply in two waves in 2025: **AI literacy and prohibited practices on 2 February**, then **general-purpose AI model obligations and governance rules on 2 August**. ([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1689&utm_source=openai))

### 2 February 2025 — AI literacy and prohibited practices

- **AI literacy (Article 4):** Under the wording that applied in 2025, providers and organisations using AI systems had to take measures, to the extent possible, to ensure sufficient AI literacy among staff and others operating or using those systems on their behalf. Article 4 was amended in 2026. ([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1689&utm_source=openai))
- **Prohibited AI practices (Article 5):** The bans covered practices such as harmful manipulation or exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, untargeted scraping of internet or CCTV images to build facial-recognition databases, and emotion recognition in workplaces and schools, subject to specified exceptions. The Act’s scope and definitions also began to apply. ([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1689&utm_source=openai))

### 2 August 2025 — General-purpose AI models and governance

- **General-purpose AI (GPAI) model providers** had to maintain technical documentation, provide information to downstream AI system providers, adopt an EU copyright compliance policy, and publish a summary of training content. Qualifying open-source models were exempt from certain documentation duties, but not from the copyright policy or public summary. Providers of models posing **systemic risk** also had to notify the Commission, evaluate their models, assess and mitigate risks, report serious incidents, and maintain cybersecurity protections. Models already on the EU market before 2 August 2025 have until **2 August 2027** to comply. ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/general-purpose-ai-obligations-under-ai-act?utm_source=openai))
- **Governance, oversight and penalties:** Rules on EU and national AI governance, bodies that assess high-risk AI systems for conformity, and confidentiality began to apply. The penalties chapter also began to apply, **except Article 101**, which covers Commission fines for GPAI model providers and applied from **2 August 2026**. ([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1689&utm_source=openai))

The main **high-risk AI system requirements** and **Article 50 transparency duties** were not part of either 2025 wave. ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act?utm_source=openai))
